title.en: The servants, the General and the escape

hook.en: The servants walk out. The General offers to send assassins. And still the enemy is sleeping in Sadao's house.

objectives.en: Describe the General's offer and why it fails
Narrate how Sadao helps the American escape

narration.en: The servants walk out. The General offers to send assassins. And still the enemy is sleeping in Sadao's house.

body.en: The servants disapprove of sheltering the enemy. Yumi refuses to wash him, so Hana does it herself, and later the servants leave the house. When Sadao is called to the General, he confesses. The General, thinking only of his own health, promises to send his private assassins to kill the man quietly and remove the body.

points.en: Yumi refuses; Hana washes him herself

We put the events in order, from the servants leaving to the escape.

say.en: Yumi refuses to wash him, so Hana does it herself.
The General promises assassins but forgets.
Sadao gives the man his boat, food and a flashlight.
No signal comes; the American has escaped.

body.en: For several nights Sadao waits, but the assassins never come: the General, absorbed in his own illness, forgets. Sadao then decides to help the American himself. He gives him his boat, food, water and clothes, and tells him to row to a small nearby island and wait for a Korean fishing boat, signalling with a flashlight if he is in trouble. No signal comes, and the man escapes.

points.en: Sadao gives boat, food and clothes

problem.en: Why did the General fail to keep his promise to Sadao?

steps.en: He promised to send private assassins.
He was absorbed in his own pain and illness.
He depended on Sadao and cared only for himself.
His forgetfulness shows selfishness, and it saves the American.

answer.en: The General promised to have the American killed by private assassins, but he forgot completely. He was so absorbed in his own pain and his fear of the coming operation that nothing else mattered. His self-centredness shows his selfish nature, and ironically it leaves Sadao free to save the American.
